newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - June 5.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - June 5.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Thursday and main factors likely to affect trading:
* The mild consolidation of Philippine shares the past two days is likely to be replicated as the market forms a solid base for the next runup, traders said.

* Lippo Securities research manager Jidgette Valenzuela said release of May inflation figures may be discounted by the market after government's announcement that is is lowering its expected target inflation for the year to between 5.2 and 5.7 percent from the earlier forecast of 6.0 and 6.5 percent.
* The National Statistics Office (NSO) said on Thursday Philippine year-on-year inflation was 4.2 percent in May as against April's 4.6 percent.
* The NSO said four-month merchandise exports rose to $7.58 billion versus $6.17 billion a year ago while April exports was at $2.08 billion as against $1.49 billion the previous year.
* On Wednesday, the Philippine Stock Exchange composite index ended 6.67 points lower at 2,796.11.
* The Dow Jones on Wednesday ended 42.49 points lower at 7,269.66. PLDT's ADR rose $0 3/8 to $59.
* The Philippine peso closed lower at 26.368 to the dollar vs 26.365.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average slipped to 16.03125 percent vs 16.0625.
* The Philippines Central Bank on Thursday cut its overnight rates by two percentage points each. Overnight borrowing rate is now 14 percent, while the lending rate is 16 percent.

* The Philippine Senate will not be able to pass a crucial tax reform bill by this week, the deadline set under an International Monetary Fund (IMF) programme, Senate ways and means committee chairman Juan Ponce Enrile said.

* Analysts said investors are not worried about the delay in Manila's exit from 30-years of IMF supervision as long as the reason for the delay - Congressional agreement on tax reforms - is sorted out.

* Metropolitan Bank and Trust Co denied rumours that one of its debtors, San Carlos Milling Co, was experiencing financial difficulties. San Carlos also denied talk that it was experiencing financial problems due to its huge inventory of imported sugar.
* Petron Corp said it will not be able to immediately conduct a review of its crude supply pact with its shareholder Saudi Arabia's Aramco because it would violate their contract.

* Australian-based soft drink bottle Coca-Cola Amatil (CCA) Ltd said it had settled the final details of its share swap deal with San Miguel Corp to create the world's second largest Coca-Cola bottler.
* Arboyne NL said it would change the company's name and increase its authorised capital ahead of the final development of the Nonoc nickel project in the Philippines.
* SM Prime Holdings said it would build a 20-hectare shopping complex on the Manila Bay reclamation area within the next three years.
* Newspaper Times Journal quoted Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo as saying the government will formally ask the IMF to extend its existing economic programme by three or four months.

* Philippine Daily Inquirer reported that banking sources said that creditors of Victorias Milling Corp are still unable to come up with a restructuring agreement for the sugar miller that has sought a 90-day moratorium on its loan interest payments. The problem was on the difficulty in forging a secondary mortgage agreement among all the 31 creditor banks.
